faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: We answer your questions before the pre-consultation.

whatIncludes.question: What does monthly operation include vs setup?
whatIncludes.answer: Setup covers the initial design, development, and integration of Servi-IA with your systems. Monthly operation covers the operated service, ongoing support, platform, maintenance, minor adjustments, and the base package of included minutes.

additionalMinutes.question: How is additional consumption charged?
additionalMinutes.answer: If you exceed the included minutes, additional consumption follows the scale: Web Conversion starts at USD 0.16/min, Voice Cloud / PBX starts at USD 0.18/min, and Enterprise is defined by volume and complexity.

secondAgent.question: How does adding a second agent work?
secondAgent.answer: A second agent is usually added with no setup fee (subject to complexity evaluation), and you get a 10% discount on the monthly fee for the second agent.

metaCosts.question: Who covers WhatsApp / Meta costs?
metaCosts.answer: Outbound or proactive messages on WhatsApp are governed by Meta's pricing and are directly covered by the client through their own card or messaging balance.

replaceTeam.question: Does this replace my team?
replaceTeam.answer: No. It automates repetitive tasks and frees your team for higher-value work. Servi-IA escalates to a human agent when the case falls outside automated scripts.

changeOperation.question: Do I need to change my current operation?
changeOperation.answer: No. We integrate with your existing infrastructure (CRM, calendars, PBX, telephony, messaging).

voiceInfra.question: Do I need to replace my current voice infrastructure?
voiceInfra.answer: No. Servi-IA can connect to your existing phone system, PBX, or voice provider when the integration is technically available.

howLong.question: How long does implementation take?
howLong.answer: It depends on the scope evaluated during the free pre-consultation. We typically define and deploy a functional pilot in weeks.

omnichannel.question: Can Servi-IA work across WhatsApp, web, and phone calls?
omnichannel.answer: Yes. We design the flow according to your channels so the agent can receive context, answer, qualify, schedule, or escalate from the touchpoints your operation uses.

handoffRequired.question: What happens when a case needs a human agent?
handoffRequired.answer: Servi-IA detects cases outside the automated flow and transfers the context to your team so the conversation can continue without starting from zero.

ownMetrics.question: Can I track my own operation metrics?
ownMetrics.answer: Yes. We can connect the agent to your CRM, dashboards, or reporting processes so you can measure conversations, outcomes, usage, and operational follow-up.

whatIsClickToIA.question: What is Click-to-Servi-IA-Call?
whatIsClickToIA.answer: It is a web or campaign flow where a visitor leaves their details and immediately connects with Servi-IA by voice, with the form context already available to the agent.

whatIsCallback.question: What is a callback with Servi-IA?
whatIsCallback.answer: It is an outbound call requested from a form or workflow. Servi-IA calls the person with the submitted context and follows the rules defined for your operation.

dataPrivacy.question: Do you handle sensitive data and regulatory compliance?
dataPrivacy.answer: Yes, for regulated sectors we have implementation processes that guarantee data sovereignty and secure storage within your ecosystem.

help.name: Enter a clear, unique internal name for this automation, for example Appointment confirmation.
help.capability: Select the channel or capability that will run the rule. In this modal it is the WhatsApp booking notification capability.
help.event: Select the event that will trigger the rule, such as a booking being created, updated, or cancelled.
help.template: Choose a WhatsApp template approved by and synchronized from Meta. Complete its parameters under Template variables.
help.recipientStrategy: Choose where the recipient comes from: the event customer, a configured group, or a specific event field.
help.recipientGroup: Enter the configured group key or the event path containing the recipient, according to the selected strategy.
help.scheduleMode: Choose whether to send the message immediately or at a time calculated relative to the booking.
help.scheduleOffset: Enter how many minutes before or after the booking to send it. Use a negative number for before and a positive number for after.
help.priority: Sets the processing order. A lower number has higher priority; keep 100 if no special order is needed.
help.enabled: Enable this so the rule can create deliveries. Disable it to save the configuration without running it.
help.conditionField: Enter the exact path of the data to evaluate, for example booking.status.
help.conditionsMode: Choose whether every condition must match or one matching condition is enough.
help.conditionOperator: Select how the field is compared with the value: equal, different, included, greater, lower, or existence.
help.conditionValue: Enter the value the condition must match. For in and not_in operators, separate multiple values with commas.
help.variableKey: Enter the number or key of the parameter expected by the Meta template, for example 1 or customer_name.
help.variableSource: Choose whether the value comes from an event field or is a fixed text value.
help.variableValue: Enter the fixed text that will replace this parameter whenever the template is sent.
help.variablePath: Enter the event data path that will fill this parameter, for example booking.start_at.
help.variableFormat: Choose how the data is transformed before insertion into the template, such as text, date, or time.
help.variableTimezone: Enter a fixed IANA timezone such as America/Bogota. Leave it empty when using a dynamic path.
help.variableTimezonePath: Enter the event path containing the timezone. Leave it empty when a fixed timezone is set.
help.variableDefault: Enter the value used when the selected path has no data.
help.variableRequired: Choose whether delivery must stop when this parameter has no available value.

form.scheduleHint: Examples: -1440 = 24 hours before, -120 = 2 hours before, -60 = 1 hour before, -30 = 30 minutes before.

appearance.logoUrl: Paste a public HTTPS URL for the logo to display. Leave it blank to use the default presentation.
appearance.color: Visually choose the primary color used for buttons and accents.
appearance.colorHex: Enter the same color as a six-digit hexadecimal value, for example #0891B2.
appearance.backgroundColor: Visually choose the background color behind the form. Leave it blank to use the selected mode's default.
appearance.backgroundColorHex: Enter the same color as a six-digit hexadecimal value, for example #F4F7F6.
appearance.colorScheme: Choose whether the form is shown in light or dark mode. Older experiences default to light.
appearance.layout: Choose how the content and form are arranged on the customer's screen.

consent.required: Enable this when the customer must explicitly accept the legal copy before continuing.
consent.label: Write the copy shown beside the consent checkbox. It is required only when consent is enabled.
consent.privacyUrl: Paste a public HTTPS URL for the applicable privacy policy.

behavior.language: Select the language the agent will use during the call.
behavior.mode: Choose WebRTC to speak in the browser, callback to call the registered phone number, or allow both so the person can pick how they want to be contacted.
behavior.phoneField: Select the required phone field that will be used as the destination.
behavior.defaultCountry: Used to interpret local numbers that do not include an international code.
behavior.auto_start: Enable this to indicate that the call should start after the context is completed.
behavior.show_microphone_help: Enable this to show the customer guidance about microphone permission.

contextSchemaFields.schemaKey: Enter a stable lowercase technical key without spaces; use letters, numbers, and underscores, for example contact_details.
contextSchemaFields.name: Give the schema a recognizable name so it can be found and reused.
contextSchemaFields.description: Summarize the information grouped by this schema and when it should be used.

contextFields.key: Enter a unique lowercase technical key without spaces, for example customer_email. It cannot be changed after creation.
contextFields.label: Enter the visible name that helps the customer understand which information is requested.
contextFields.fieldType: Choose the data format so the correct control and validation can be applied.
contextFields.collectionMode: Choose whether the value is requested, prefilled, confirmed, kept internal, or collected during the call.
contextFields.description: Add a short explanation of the information the customer should provide.
contextFields.sensitivity: Mark data as sensitive when it requires more careful handling.
contextFields.required: Enable this when the customer must provide the value before continuing.
contextFields.options: Add one option per line using value|Label. At least one is required for select fields.
contextFields.validation: Add advanced rules as a valid JSON object. Leave it blank when no additional validation is needed.
